### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **61** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**39** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d795719926a2dacf7a394e23b717f36961343a26`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **11** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **33** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d795719926a2dacf7a394e23b717f36961343a26` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1a058c00c3aa2ff0b3007b8940a254a4b38a6ea8` — the merge of head `d75ae9784332b0ba3d0eeb48efb8d1ee978eed5c` into base `d795719926a2dacf7a394e23b717f36961343a26`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1a058c00c3aa2ff0b3007b8940a254a4b38a6ea8 && git checkout 1a058c00c3aa2ff0b3007b8940a254a4b38a6ea8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d795719926a2dacf7a394e23b717f36961343a26 d75ae9784332b0ba3d0eeb48efb8d1ee978eed5c && git checkout -B drift-repro d795719926a2dacf7a394e23b717f36961343a26 && git merge --no-ff d75ae9784332b0ba3d0eeb48efb8d1ee978eed5c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d795719926a2dacf7a394e23b717f36961343a26
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d795719926a2dacf7a394e23b717f36961343a26` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `70ff93d3b03432d2b930d17e2605590f4a174e74`
Local-runs: none

Rendered at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` by the ruling's item 5 (`6205262047` on #23731, letter B, maintainer 「B (推荐)」); the face is the `Clause-②: yes` declaration (no `packages/spec/src/**` path, no governed path on the file list), so the tier named above is the face's. Read in this act: card #23731's body and all 10 comments; PR #23814's body, file list (28 paths) and net diff against `main` (merge base `609d07a7d`); the 40 check-runs on the head, latest per name. Scope: every path of the code diff (the two new plugin-audit modules, `activity-field-redaction.ts`, `activity-read-visibility.ts`, `audit-writers.ts`, `parent-field-query-guard.ts`, `objects/sys-activity.object.ts`, `index.ts`, the four generated translations, the five plugin-audit tests, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/activity-changed-fields.ts` with its test and three family registrations, the dogfood pin) plus, read on `origin/main`: `parent-record-read-gate.ts`, `served-fields.ts`, `comment-access-hooks.ts`, `stored-metadata-body-migration.ts`, `cli/.../migrate/audit-metadata-bodies.ts`, `cli/src/utils/absent-table-reads.ts`, `data-migration-plugins.ts`, `objectql/src/engine.ts` and `validation/rule-validator.ts` (the readonly strips), `plugin-security/src/system-write-guard.ts`, `driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` and `core/src/utils/json-membership-sql.ts`, `spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts`, ADR-0139, `scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs`. The changeset's prose and the docs are the lane seat's ACCEPT except the changeset's `Clause-②:` line and level, judged under ②. Stamp of this act: 2026-10-16T04:55Z.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The two columns on the platform object `sys_activity` — right.** `changed_fields` (`type: 'tags'`, `readonly`, not required) and `milestone_key` (`Field.text`, `readonly`, not required), both under the `Context` group, both arriving through the ordinary schema sync (measured on the rotation shard in `activity-changed-fields.integration.test.ts`, cases 1 and 2). `changed_fields` is served narrowed to the reader's served members; `milestone_key` is deleted from every row the redaction reaches (`redactActivityRows`, before the parent check) and is therefore never served to a reader the redaction runs for. Both are `NULL` when unstamped, and `[]` is stored as a value, not as `NULL`, which the stamped conjunct relies on.
- **The exported backfill — right.** `backfillActivityChangedFields(engine, logger, { apply, pageSize })` and `ACTIVITY_BACKFILL_PAGE_SIZE`, with the two report/engine types, `planActivityStamp`, the two column constants and `ActivityStamp`, all added to `src/index.ts`. It is the shape of `migrateStoredMetadataBodyCopies`: SYSTEM-context read and single-id SYSTEM update through the engine (the append-only object's migration door, never the CRUD write path), dry run by default, no `sys_migration` flag, keyset paging on `id` over `changed_fields $null: true`, both columns in one `update`. Idempotent by construction (a stamped row leaves the unstamped set; an unjudged row stays in it and is counted each run). A refused page read is counted as a failure and the door exits 1 — the pin `a read the table refuses is a failure, never a clean report` holds it.
- **The read rule, both halves, against letter B and ADR-0139 D4 — right.** `keptRowsOfParent(P, served, watched)` is, per parent, `object_name = P AND changed_fields IS NOT NULL AND (changed_fields $empty OR one $contains per served field) AND (milestone_key IS NULL, or, only when the reader is served every field of P's CURRENT `activityMilestones` declaration, milestone_key IS NULL OR milestone_key = key(current declaration))`. The update half is D4's sentence exactly (a non-empty `changed_fields` none of whose members is served is withheld; `[]` for a create, a delete, a note and an internal-only update is kept). The milestone half is the ruling's item 1 exactly (key equality against the CURRENT declaration AND every watched field served; otherwise withheld; an object with no current declaration serves no milestone row). The unstamped conjunct is D4's unjudged-row answer (fail closed). `computeWithheldRowFilter` ORs one branch per parent the read gate enumerates (`enumerateParentObjects(engine, ACTIVITY_GATE)`, the gate's own exclusions), or the one parent the read pins (`pinnedParentObject`, the query guard's reading); a parent the service gives no answer for is kept whole; no answer for any parent returns `null` (nothing narrowed). An engine with no registry view is denied once and loudly. The predicate compiles to exact membership on driver-sql: `tags` is in `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES`, which `JSON_COLUMN_TYPES` spreads, so `$contains` takes `jsonMembershipPredicate` (SQLite `json_each`, PostgreSQL's jsonb containment operator, MySQL `JSON_CONTAINS`) and `$empty` the `multi_value` arm, on all three modelled dialects; a served field that is a prefix of a withheld one cannot match.
- **No SYSTEM-composed read or leaf remains in the rule — right.** The redaction no longer imports `CommentAccessEngine`'s `find` or `PARENT_GATE_SCAN_LIMIT`; `ActivityRedactionEngine` is the registry view plus `getSchema`. The one SYSTEM read left on the stream is the read gate's own D5 bounded probe of the parent pair, which is ADR-0139 D5's and not this card's; the dogfood pin asserts exactly that and that no SYSTEM read carries a `ReadableIds` leaf. The 2,000-row window is gone from the rule (`activity-withheld-row-predicate.dogfood`: a member served past the window with one `total` on every page; an administrator's top-20 newest with `total` past the window).
- **The redaction and the query guard cover both columns — right.** `VALUE_BEARING_COLUMNS` carries both, so the fail-closed strip takes them too (`activity-predicate-guard.test.ts` pins it); `ACTIVITY_QUERY_GUARD.columns` spreads `ACTIVITY_STAMPED_COLUMNS`, so a predicate, sort, group or aggregation over either is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 to a reader withheld a parent field (pinned, matching and non-matching probes, `find` and `count`).
- **A writer cannot set either column — right.** On insert, the `sys_activity` before-insert hook assigns the planner's answer over whatever any writer sent, in every context (pinned with a SYSTEM-context insert carrying its own values). The engine's create-side static-readonly strip returns no subject for a `sys_` object (`staticReadonlyInsertSubject`), so `readonly: true` is NOT what guards the columns on insert — the hook is, as the PR says, the `is_edited` precedent. On update, a user-context write to an `append-only` object is refused by plugin-security's engine-owned write guard (ADR-0103) wherever the security service is composed; the backfill's SYSTEM update is the one sanctioned writer. The mirror and the hook stamp only when the registered `sys_activity` declares both columns (the `organization_id` precedent), read per call.
- **The CRUD mirror's stamp — right.** `planActivityStamp(activityMetadata)` over the same `{ old, new, kind, text_sources }` the row records; the watched list a fired milestone declares now comes from `declaredMilestoneWatchedFields(objectDef)`, the same function the rule keys the CURRENT declaration by, with the same `asked` predicate (`field` and `summary` strings) `matchMilestone` used on `main`, so a row written under the declaration in force compares equal.
- **The door `os migrate activity-changed-fields` — right.** Flags one for one with `audit-metadata-bodies` (`--database-url`, `--apply`, `--yes`, `--force`, `--json`), dry run by default on the read-only boot (`deferSchemaDdl` + `readOnlyProbe`), `absentTableReads` for the rotation-managed table, a non-zero `failures` count exits 1, registered in the one-shot family table, the JSON-purity family and the absent-database roster. The spelling objectstack-ai/cloud#2900 reads is unchanged.
- **The derived gate families on this head — one WRONG.** Check-runs, latest per name, none pending at the final read of this act: 34 success (all six `Test Core` shards among them), 5 skipped (Console Pin Gate, the dogfood matrix shards and Verify CLI, packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), and two `failure`: `Lint · docs & code guards` and its aggregate `Lint & Repo Gates`. The red step is `ADR symbol anchors resolve (no line numbers survive)` (`scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs`). Cause, read deterministically off the diff and `docs/adr/0139-engine-internal-semi-join-leaf-readable-parent-ids.md` on `main`: the diff deletes `computeWithheldUpdateFilter` and `isWithheldOnlyUpdate` from `activity-field-redaction.ts` (replaced by `computeWithheldRowFilter` and `keptRowsOfParent`), and ADR-0139 anchors both — line 73 (consumer table, row 3, `#computeWithheldUpdateFilter`) and line 191 (D4, `#isWithheldOnlyUpdate`); neither symbol occurs on the head, so both are `[unresolved-symbol]`. The PR body's accept-set claim that the ADR could be left alone because it is Tier H is wrong as landed: the gate reads the ADR's anchors against the tree, so a rename of an anchored symbol is a change the anchor must follow. The gate's own remedy text: update the anchor (re-point it to where the mechanism now lives) — a `docs/adr/**` edit, Tier H under Prime Directive #14 (one Tier H path makes the whole PR Tier H, so it is the maintainer's word on this PR or a sibling PR landed first) — or keep the two symbol names resolvable in the file; ⛔ never an `anchor-exempt` marker, which is maintainer-only and not for a live anchor. The other anchors into touched files (`audit-writers.ts#AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS`, `#auditRow`, `#diff`; `activity-read-visibility.ts#installActivityReadVisibility`) resolve on the head.
- **Observations, not reasons (the lane's call):** (a) an unpinned read builds one `$contains` leaf per served field per enumerated parent, each an EXISTS, jsonb-containment or `JSON_CONTAINS` construct, so the WHERE of an administrator's header-bell read grows with parents times fields; measured with one parent in the dogfood, named in the PR body, not measured on an app-sized registry. (b) The pins' field names (`awp_open` / `awp_secret`, `f_open` / `f_admin`) cannot tell membership from substring; the membership reading is established by driver-sql's construct, not by a pin — one served field that is a prefix of a withheld one would pin it. (c) In a composition with no security service the rule and the redaction do not run, so `milestone_key` is served there to context-less callers; consistent with the module's standing rule and the no-answer case, stated under ③ Q2.

### ② Semver level

`minor` for `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/cli` matches what the diff publishes: two columns on a published platform object, new package exports (the backfill, the planner, the constants and types), a new CLI subcommand, no removal from any public surface (on `main`, `src/index.ts` exports nothing from `activity-field-redaction.ts`, so `computeWithheldUpdateFilter`, `isWithheldOnlyUpdate`, `isWithheldMilestone`, `isWithheldRow` and `ActivityRedactionEngine` were package-internal, as the changeset says). `Clause-②: yes` on the PR body and on the changeset, no arm, and `yes` takes at least `minor` — right; not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. The ruling's item 3 binds the changeset's FIRST paragraph and the first paragraph carries it whole: the rollout consequence (rows written before the upgrade are withheld from every non-system reader until the backfill runs), the door `os migrate activity-changed-fields`, dry run by default, `--apply` to write, idempotent, both columns in one run, "run at once after upgrading", plus the measured difference (a dry run on a database no upgraded process has opened exits 1). Item 1's cost (older-declaration and since-removed-field milestone rows withheld until retention, 14 days declared, `lifecycle.retention_overrides` may lengthen it) is stated. `packages/qa/dogfood` is not a released package.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Q1 (the planner's stamp always overrides a writer-sent value) — A, right.** It is a superset of the ruling's "for any writer that does not": every writer is stamped, and a writer that stamps is re-derived. B would let any server action relax the read rule for its own rows, which the ruling's floor forbids (item 2: "a row the planner cannot judge stays unstamped and fails closed" presumes the planner's answer is the row's). Pinned (ablation A6; the SYSTEM-context insert carrying `changed_fields: []` and a key reads back `null` / `null`).
- **Q2 (no security service, or no field answer for a parent: unstamped rows not withheld) — A, right on the merits.** The ruling's item 3 sentence "withheld from every non-system reader" is the rollout consequence for a served deployment, where every non-system reader is one the security service answers for; a parent the service gives no answer for has no withheld field to protect, and the module's standing rule — "a reader the service gives no answer for is narrowed by neither", restated in `permissions/system-context.mdx` row 45 — already serves such a reader every row whole, withheld updates and milestones included. Withholding unstamped rows there would empty every feed of a security-less composition and protect nothing; it relaxes no access boundary, because none exists where no field answer exists. The changeset's paragraph holds for every deployment that composes the security service (the cloud v18 move among them). Accepted.
- **Deviation 1 (docs and generated surfaces outside the claim's list) — accepted:** `deployment/cli.mdx`, `system-context.mdx` row 45, the tenant-audit census (225 to 226, the backfill's `update` is the new site) and `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json` (16 to 17) are gate-regenerated or the lane's prose; the translations are the i18n gates' regeneration (green).
- **Deviation 2 (three family registrations) — right:** a new `migrate` door must join the one-shot family table, the JSON-purity family and the absent-database roster, or those suites red.
- **Deviation 3 (`ACTIVITY_GATE` exported; the #21388 header rewritten) — right:** the rule enumerates parents through the gate's own enumeration, one source of truth.
- **Deviations 4 to 7** (package-local tsc and check runs outside the verify lock; the detached primary checkout; the model-free trailer pair; one merge of `origin/main`) — process notes consistent with AGENTS.md; nothing to answer.
- **The out-of-scope finding (stale prose in `parent-record-read-gate.ts` and ADR-0139's consumer row 3) — escalated, not noted:** the ADR half of it is exactly the anchor that reds this head (①, FAIL reason). `parent-record-read-gate.ts`'s `no-object-admission` prose stays #23732's / #22788's. The report's gate line "`pnpm check:adr-anchors` exited 0" names the presence gate (`check-adr-anchors.mjs`), not the symbol gate (`check:adr-symbol-anchors`), and the 103-gate union did not carry the red one; CI did.
- **CI at the final read of this act:** every check completed; all six `Test Core` shards green; every other check green or skipped except the two named reds, which share the one cause above.
